title: Model Onboard Regression Synthesis Brief 2026-06-18
content:
Summary:
This brief aggregates the primary regression and improvement signals observed during model onboarding runs for two open models (redwood-7b-v2 and community-13b-compact) across three runtime changes we rolled into the canary lane between 2026-06-09 and 2026-06-17: 1) fallback of new flash-attn microkernel (fa-v3 -> fa-v2 revert-ish), 2) paged KV allocator adjustments (paged-kv: page-size and eviction policy), and 3) continuous batching tuning (cont-batch v2: target-latency tradeoff). Purpose is to synthesize diffs, propose root causes, and recommend immediate mitigations for onboarding windows.

Background/context:
- Onboarding runs are the standard prompt-set based evals used to gate model availability in hosted API + dedicated ramp. We execute ~10 prompt families (see Prompt sets below) and capture: token-latency P50/P95, throughput (tok/s), model-side mem pressure, perplexity on held-out evals, and downstream quality signals (QA exact match, reranking NDCG@5, hallucination flag rate).
- Canary lane received three changes together last week to reduce cost and tail latency for long-history chat: flash-attn microkernel update, paged-KV eviction tweak (keep-hot windows 2x), and continuous-batching aggressiveness bump.

Testbeds and config snapshot:
- Hardware: gpunode-x1 (A100-80GB equiv) and gpunode-s1 (H100-96GB equiv) mixed; most anomalies observed on A100 class.
- Runtime: runtime@2026-06-09+canary, kernel bundle: fa-v3 (new), paged-kv: eviction=LRU-window-2, cont-batch: target-latency-ms=80 (was 60).
- Model pins: redwood-7b-v2@v2026-06-01, community-13b-compact@v2026-05-28.

Prompt sets (short):
- long-chat-history-regen (12 prompts, 2k prefix lengths)
- small-qna-lookup (short prompts, ref doc lookup)
- math-step-by-step (structured output, verification)
- summarization-med (500–800 tokens)
- safety-probes (adversarial prompts)

Key signals (high level):
- Latency: P95 increased by 18–28% on long-chat-history-regen for redwood-7b-v2 on A100 when fa-v3 was active; P50 roughly unchanged.
- Throughput: tokens/s fell 9% under cont-batch v2 for small-batch short prompts (unexpected; expected higher batching to increase throughput).
- Memory: paged-KV adjustments reduced peak GPU mem by ~6% for community-13b-compact but increased CPU-side paging events (observed +3x page faults) during high-concurrency runs.
- Quality: small but consistent drop in structural-verification exact-match on math-step-by-step for redwood-7b-v2 (-1.6% abs), not present on community-13b-compact.
- Hallucination: safety-probes produced 0.4% higher flagged hallucination rate for redwood-7b-v2 under the fa-v3 kernel.

Detailed diffs (representative):
- redwood-7b-v2, long-chat-history-regen, A100:
  - baseline (fa-v2, paged-kv old, cont-batch 60): P50=28ms, P95=190ms, throughput=12.2k tok/s
  - canary (fa-v3, paged-kv w2, cont-batch 80): P50=30ms, P95=235ms, throughput=11.1k tok/s
  - delta: P95 +45ms (+24%), throughput -9%

- community-13b-compact, summarization-med, A100:
  - baseline: P50=62ms, P95=430ms, throughput=6.1k tok/s, peak-gpu-mem=36.2GB
  - canary: P50=61ms, P95=410ms, throughput=6.3k tok/s, peak-gpu-mem=34.0GB
  - delta: P95 -20ms, mem -2.2GB, throughput +3%

Hypotheses / probable causes:
1) Flash-attn microkernel regression: fa-v3 introduced a fallback code-path for certain head counts and sequence lengths that trips under long prefix + KV paged layout; this increases tail latency but not median. Evidence: p95 skew, increased CPU->GPU stalls in profiling traces, and correlation with prompts that use KV heavily.
2) Continuous-batching aggressiveness mismatch: raising target-latency allowed larger batches, but for short prompt patterns (small-qna-lookup) the scheduler coalesces too eagerly, increasing per-request scheduling jitter and small-request throughput drop. The scheduling algorithm does not currently decouple short vs long prefix workload shapes.
3) Paged-KV eviction policy tradeoff: keeping more 'hot' pages in GPU reduced average memory pressure for big models, but increased CPU-side bookkeeping and occasional page-resident misses when concurrency spikes, causing kernel fallbacks (see hypothesis 1) to execute more frequently.

Evidence collected / reproducibility notes:
- Repro script: ./ci/onboard_regress/run_single_eval.sh --model redwood-7b-v2 --promptset long-chat-history-regen --runtime-tag canary-fa-v3 --profile perf-trace-2026-06-12 (artifact attached in CON-1132).
- Perf traces: flamegraphs show fa-v3 path spending ~1.9x more time inside kernel fallback for headcount mismatch cases.
- Paging stats: /var/log/paged-kv shows spike aligned with concurrency bursts (2026-06-12 02:13Z).

Immediate mitigations (recommended order):
- Roll back fa-v3 microkernel from canary lane for A100-class nodes while we triage (quick rollback, low blast radius).
- Revert cont-batch target-latency to 60ms for short-prompt-heavy pools (route small-qna-lookup traffic to cont-batch v1 policy).
- Restore paged-KV eviction window to previous setting; schedule staged experiment on H100s only to validate mem/throughput gains.

Planned investigations and owners:
- Kernel engineer deep-dive on fa-v3 fallback condition (owner: Ravi Menon, ETA 2026-06-21).
- Scheduler tweak proposal: introduce request-shape heuristic to decouple short vs long prefix (owner: Elena Gomez, prototype due 2026-06-25).
- Paged-KV telemetry: add per-request page fault tagging to traces so we can correlate with kernel fallback (owner: Jonah Reed, PR in progress).

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Why did community-13b-compact see throughput gains while redwood-7b-v2 regressed? Model architecture differences or size+headcount interplay? Need headcount/attn-dim matrix test.
- Is there any interaction with quantization profiles (we used q4f16 for 7b and q5_0 for 13b-compact)? Could microkernel pick different code-path due to quantization encoding?
- Can we simulate high-concurrency page storm in a unit test harness? If so, add to nightly regression.

Next actions (short list):
- Rollback fa-v3 on A100 canary (Ops) — DONE 2026-06-18 11:40 UTC (monitoring).
- Re-run onboarding suite with fa-v2 + cont-batch v2 to isolate cont-batch effect (Maya + Elena).
- Patch runtime to emit page-fault tag in traces (Jonah) and create dashboard tile for page-fault correlation.

Appendix: quick checklist for release gating
- [ ] Confirm P95 back within 10% of baseline across long-chat-history-regen on A100s
- [ ] Verify math-step-by-step exact-match recovered to within 0.5% abs
- [ ] No increase in flagged hallucination rate on safety-probes
- [ ] Perf traces show <1.2x fallback kernel time vs baseline

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence catalog: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AM/Onboard+Eval+Catalog
- Runtime PR that rolled fa-v3: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1294
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-4827 (kernel fallback investigation)
- Trace artifact: CON-1132 (perf-traces-2026-06-12)

If you want a narrow repro to run locally: ping me and I will share the short dockerized harness (contains prebuilt model shards and pinned runtime).

-- maya

Unresolved: check whether release notes for quantization included any microkernel ABI change that we missed; flagged to release-engineering.
